post.description:
Check the username and password and start a session. After MAX_FAILED_LOGINS wrong passwords in a row, the
account is locked for LOCK_MINUTES: even the right password is refused until then.
A second step follows the right password for some accounts: the code from their authenticator app, or for the
roles in EMAIL_CODE_ROLES a code emailed to them (core/email_codes.py). Asking again without a code sends a new one.
Start setting up two-factor sign-in: a new secret for the authenticator app (not in use until confirmed).
Confirm with a code from the app: from now on, signing in needs the password and a code.
Turn two-factor sign-in off, with your password and a current code (not allowed where your role requires it).
Sign out everywhere: every login token this account has stops working, and this browser's cookie is removed.

get.description: The signed-in user's own account.

post.description:
Replace your password. You must know the current one. Every other device is signed out; this one gets a new
session.
Choose a different username. You must confirm with your current password.

get.description: Your account and your work details (read-only): department, manager and, for managers, team size.

patch.description: Change your name, email, phone or job title. A new email address triggers an alert to the old one.

put.description: How routine emails arrive: each as it happens, or one digest each morning. Account emails always come at once.
Close the first-time guide on the overview, or show it again.
Set or remove your profile picture (a small image, already shrunk by the browser).

get.description: Your most recent notifications, newest first, and how many are unread.

post.description: Mark your notifications read (these ones, or all).

get.description: Every account, sorted by name.

schema.title: Response List Users Api Admin Users Get

post.description:
Create an account with a temporary password and send the welcome email with the sign-in details. The person
must choose their own password at first sign-in (and may change their username then).

patch.description: Change an account's username, name or email address. The person signs in with the new username.

delete.description:
Delete an account for good. Not allowed for your own account, or for an account that appears in the decision
log (it recommended someone or decided on a promotion): deleting it would erase who made those decisions, so
deactivate it instead. A manager's team members stay in the directory, without a manager. Activity-log
entries keep the person's name.

patch.description: Deactivate an account (the person can no longer sign in) or reactivate it.

Let an Admin account view employees' records and scores (read-only), or stop it. Only Admin accounts can be
given this: HR already sees everyone, and employees and managers see what their role allows.

post.description: Give a user a new temporary password, e.g. when they have forgotten theirs. It is emailed to them too.

put.description:
Make exactly these employees the manager's team. People removed from the list no longer have a manager
until they are given one; people on someone else's team move to this manager.

get.description:
The employee directory as the admin needs it to link logins and build teams: names, departments, managers.
No scores or work records: admins manage accounts, not promotions.
The latest 500 entries, newest first; filter by action, or search names and details.
Whether a mail server is set up (never the password itself), and how many emails are in the outbox.

post.description: Send a test email, to check the settings work. Waits for the answer, so the admin sees any problem.

get.description: The 100 most recent emails: to whom, the subject, whether they were delivered, attempts and any error.

post.description: Try a failed (or only saved) email again now.
Send any reminders that are due now (the scheduler also does this every hour). Each goes out only once.

get.description: The 30 most recent saved (not sent) emails: who to, the subject and the plain-text body.

Everything the admin's dashboard shows, from the live system: accounts by role, recent activity, the model
(version, training date, a timed test prediction), the fairness check, drift, and email. Only totals and
distributions: no employee's record or score.
The employees this user may see, each with their readiness score.

post.description:
"Run predictions for everyone": score every employee this user may see with the live model, now, and say when.
Nothing is saved: the scores are worked out from the current records each time.

get.description:
Score, exact contributions (SHAP), plain-language summary and the what-if options, at once. LIME's rules are
included when they're already worked out for this record; otherwise "lime" is empty (start it with
POST /employees/{id}/lime).
Who the employee is, without running the model (the page shows this before "Run prediction" is clicked).

post.description:
Run the model now: the score and each factor's exact contribution, the summary and the what-if options.
The page calls this when someone clicks "Run prediction"; LIME and the tips follow as separate steps.

The second opinion: start LIME for this employee (or get the result if it's already worked out). 200 with the
rules and fit when ready; 202 while it runs; then ask again with GET.

get.description: LIME's result for this employee's current record and the live model: 200 when ready, 202 while it runs.

post.description: The score and explanation if some improvable inputs were different. Nothing is saved.

get.description: The smallest realistic improvements that would reach the threshold.

Which inputs matter most across all employees (measured on the training sample), and every piece of
information the model is never given, with the reason.

put.description: HR sets the range managers propose within.

get.description:
HR sees every nomination; a manager sees the ones they made, and any made for their own team by a manager
covering for them. Newest first.

post.description: A manager recommends one of their own team members (or of a team they're covering) for promotion.
HR approves (with the final pay rise) or rejects. Disagreeing with the model needs a 20-character reason.
HR answers Finance: a revised (or the same) pay rise, with a note. It goes back to Finance.

get.description:
Every decision, newest first. HR, and the compliance auditor (read-only). `pay_status` keeps only those at one
step of Finance's sign-off (the notification bell asks only for the ones Finance sent back).

An employee's approved promotions: new role, start date and pay rise. Pending nominations aren't shown, and
nor are approvals whose pay rise Finance hasn't signed off yet.

Every promotion pay rise that has been through Finance (waiting first, oldest waiting first; then newest), with
a summary. `cycle_id` keeps only one review cycle's.

post.description: Finance confirms the pay rise. The promotion is now final: the manager and the employee are told.

Sign off several pay rises at once: only ones waiting for Finance and within the pay policy (a rise outside the
policy is always reviewed on its own). Each is signed off, logged and announced exactly as if done one by one.
Finance sends the pay rise back to HR with a reason. Nobody else is told.

get.description: Signed-off promotion pay rises for payroll (only those not yet handed over, unless include_sent).

post.description: Finance confirms these signed-off rises were handed to payroll. Each can be marked once.

get.description: The range HR set (Finance can read it, not change it).
Everything the form and the CSV template need: the fields, departments and managers.

post.description: Add one employee to the directory. They can be scored at once, and linked to a login by the admin.

get.description: One employee's details in the units HR types in, for the edit form.

put.description: Update an employee's details, e.g. after a new review. Past decisions keep the score they were made with.

get.description: Every change to this employee's work record, newest first.

post.description:
Check a CSV file of employees, row by row; with save=True, add them all.
All or nothing: if any row has an error, no one is added, so a file is never half-imported.

get.description: The open cycle's name, model and nomination deadline, or null. For every signed-in page.
Every cycle, newest first, each with its headline totals.

post.description: HR opens a cycle: everyone is scored with the live model now, and the scores are saved. One at a time.

get.description: How a cycle is going. HR sees the people it concerns; the auditor sees totals only.

post.description: HR closes the open cycle, once every nomination in it has been decided.

get.description: HR: one row per employee in the cycle: their saved score, and what happened to any nomination.
One employee's saved score in every review cycle, oldest first: to them, their manager and HR.
Every manager (with who they report to, their team and any cover today), and everyone without a manager.

put.description: HR puts these employees under a manager (moving them from any other team), or under nobody.

get.description: The active managers' names, to choose who covers (names only).
Covers now and coming up. A manager sees the ones they give or receive; HR sees all.

post.description: While a manager is away, another manager sees and may nominate their team. At most 6 months; no overlaps.
End a cover early (or cancel one that hasn't started): the manager who is away, the cover, or HR.

get.description: The numbers the landing page shows, straight from the last training and evaluation runs.
Your rating of the explanation from the current model, if you have given one.

post.description:
Rate your explanation. Stored with the model version and the score it explained (worked out here, not taken
from the page). Rating the same model's explanation again replaces your earlier rating. Never changes a score.

get.description: The values in your work record you can ask HR to correct, with what the record says now.

post.description: Ask HR to correct one value in your record. HR checks the evidence; nothing changes until HR confirms.
Attach one file (PDF, JPEG or PNG, up to 10 MB) to your pending request. A new file replaces the old one.

get.description: Your correction requests, newest first, with HR's decisions.
HR's decisions on your correction requests that you haven't seen yet.

post.description: You've seen the decisions on your record.

get.description: Every correction request: waiting ones first (oldest first), then decided ones (newest first).

post.description:
HR checked the evidence and confirms the value they verified (which may differ from the one asked for). The
record is corrected, the employee re-scored, and both scores logged with the model version.
HR keeps the record as it is, with a reason (at least 20 characters) that the employee receives.

get.description:
Pending corrections to the nominee's record (the score may change), and whether the decision is on hold. While
it is, the decision API refuses a decision (app/promotion/routes_decisions.py).

post.description: Hold the decision until the nominee's pending corrections are resolved. Not a decision, and not an override.
Take the decision off hold without waiting for the correction.

get.description:
How employees rated their explanations, in aggregate only: the share rating clarity and usefulness 4 or 5 (shown
only from MIN_GROUP ratings), and how often each factor was marked wrong or unfair. Never one person's rating.
The dashboard's numbers for these filters, and the filter options.
The same numbers as a CSV file (section, measure, value), with the same small-group protection.
Every trained version, newest first: which is live, which wait for release, which are blocked.

get.description: One version's model card and its release history.

Before releasing: both this version and the live model score today's employees. How many each recommends, who
would gain or lose a recommendation, how far scores move, per department. Nothing is saved. HR only (names).

post.description:
Make this version the live model, after reading its card. HR only, with a note of at least 20 characters.
Releasing an older version is how a release is rolled back. With FOUR_EYES on, this asks a second HR person.

get.description:
The four-fifths rule on today's directory and decisions: the model, managers' nominations and HR's approvals.

The audit trail, newest first, 50 per page; filter by event, or by what it is about.
Recompute every hash: is the trail exactly as it was written?

post.description: A new participant: their code, and the facilitator's link (shown once; only its hash is kept).

report it writes (results/user_test.md).

The participant's questionnaire. Every statement needs an answer from 1 to 5; then the link stops working.

get.description: How long each kind of personal data is kept (public: shown on the privacy page).
Everything the platform holds about you, as one JSON file (to keep, or to ask questions about).
